outlook.statement: Ground water recharge in command areas encouraging for cane planting, supporting factory operations for at least next two years. Competitive crops with remunerative prices could pose threat to sugarcane cultivation. Government allowed export of 1.5 million tons in sugar season 2025-26. Ambitious ethanol program continues to be supportive. Draft rules proposed in April 2026 for higher ethanol blends including E85 and E100. Government policy on sugar will continue to have significant bearing on industry prospects.
outlook.period: Next two years and coming years

outlook.statement: The Board perceives the risk of recurring lower sugar recovery in the State of Tamil Nadu as compared to minimum recovery for which sugar mills are to pay the Fair and Remunerative Price. Lower capacity utilization is also a concern. The Tamil Nadu Industry has also the option of producing Ethanol. The Tamil Nadu Government has issued an Ethanol Blending Policy 2023 to attract investments in molasses/grain-based ethanol programme to make the state self-sufficient in meeting the estimated annual requirement of 130 crore litres. However, the State has the limited scope as availability of molasses is limited. The Tamil Nadu government has been allowing the manufacturers of Indian Made Foreign Liquor to import a major share of the requirement of Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) (raw material for processing into liquor) from other neighboring states, giving an unfair advantage to the other states due to comparatively lower rate of taxes. This has an adverse effect in the cash flow stream of sugar manufacturers in the state of Tamil Nadu, as ENA is also one of the main streams of revenue.

The country is set to produce 29.29 million tons in the current season 2025-26. With an export possibility of 0.7 million tons and a consumption figure at 28.3 million tons, it would leave the industry with a closing stock at 5.29 million tons.

The Board of Directors have considered the financial position of the Company as at 31st March, 2026 and projected cash flows and financial performance of the Company for at least twelve months from the date of approval of these financial statements as well as planned cost and cash improvement actions, and believe that the plan for sustained profitability remains on course.
outlook.period: at least twelve months from the date of approval of these financial statements

outlook.statement: The Board of Directors of the Company are of the considered view that the Company would be able to generate adequate profits in the immediate future as soon as the cane availability position improves and reaches normal levels.

Interest rate risk: A fall in the discount rate linked to Government Securities increases the present value of gratuity liability.
Salary Risk: Increase in member salaries beyond assumed levels increases the plan's liability.
Investment Risk: Return on plan assets below the discount rate creates a plan deficit.
Asset Liability Matching Risk: Risk of matching cash flows, though mitigated by investment in lines of Rule 101 of Income Tax Rules, 1962.
Mortality risk: No longevity risk as benefits are payable only till retirement age.
Concentration Risk: All plan assets invested with insurance companies; a default would wipe out all assets, though probability is low due to stringent regulatory guidelines.
